138- *  Direct manipulation of the pix data field
139- *  -----------------------------------------
140- *
141- *  Memory management of the (image) data field in the pix is
142- *  handled differently from that in the colormap or text fields.
143: *  For colormap and text, the functions pixSetColormap() and
144- *  pixSetText() remove the existing heap data and insert the
145- *  new data.  For the image data, pixSetData() just reassigns the
146- *  data field; any existing data will be lost if there isn't
147- *  another handle for it.
148- *
149- *  Why is pixSetData() limited in this way?  Because the image
150- *  data can be very large, we need flexible ways to handle it,
151- *  particularly when you want to re-use the data in a different
152- *  context without making a copy.  Here are some different
153- *  things you might want to do:
154- *
155- *  (1) Use pixCopy(pixd, pixs) where pixd is not the same size
156- *      as pixs.  This will remove the data in pixd, allocate a
157- *      new data field in pixd, and copy the data from pixs, leaving
158- *      pixs unchanged.
159- *
160- *  (2) Use pixTransferAllData(pixd, &pixs, ...) to transfer the
161- *      data from pixs to pixd without making a copy of it.  If
162- *      pixs is not cloned, this will do the transfer and destroy pixs.
163- *      But if the refcount of pixs is greater than 1, it just copies
